chunks: Abān narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who owes a debt until a specified term, then his creditor comes to him and says: “Pay me such-and-such from what is owed to me, and I will remit the rest for you,” or he says: “Pay me part of it, and I will extend the term for you regarding what remains.”
So he عليه السلام said: “I do not see any harm in it, so long as he does not add anything to his principal.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Then you shall have your principal sums; you shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged.”

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: A specified term or fixed deadline for repayment.
key_terms.انْقُدْ: Pay in cash or make immediate payment.
key_terms.بَقِيَّتَهُ: Its remainder; the rest of the outstanding amount.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A debt owed by one person to another.
key_terms.رَأْسِ مَالِهِ: His principal amount, without any increase.
key_terms.رُءُوسُ أَمْوَالِكُمْ: Your principal sums, meaning the original capital only.
key_terms.غَرِيمُهُ: His creditor; the one to whom the debt is owed.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to settle a debt early for a reduced amount or extend the term without increasing the principal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on debt settlement before the due date. It permits reducing part of a debt in exchange for earlier payment, or rearranging payment timing, so long as nothing is added above the principal amount. The Imam عليه السلام supports this ruling with the Qur’anic principle that one is entitled only to the principal without committing or suffering injustice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3270 - Aban narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who reported from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) regarding a man who owes a debt with a specified due date.
The creditor comes to him and says, "Pay me such-and-such amount from what you owe, and I will waive the rest," or says, "Pay me a part now, and I will extend the deadline for the remainder."
Imam (as) said: "I see no harm in it, as long as nothing is added to the principal amount."
Allah (swt), the Almighty, says: 'Then you shall have your principal; you shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged.' (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:279)"
